s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual disturbance in a patient with a history of breast cancer and recent initiation of hormonal therapy
salient_findings: Parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
History of hypertension
History of stage IA estrogen receptor–positive and progesterone receptor–positive and ERBB/neu receptor–negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast
Started receiving 1 mg of anastrozole daily 6 months prior to presentation
Not using any other notable medications
Denied any recent changes to her regimen
Never previously used tamoxifen
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/40 OD and 20/25 OS
Pupils were equal, round, and reactive without an afferent pupillary defect
Intraocular pressures were normal
Anterior segment examination was only notable for mild cataracts in both eyes
Fundus examination was notable for parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in the right and left eyes

raw.rationale: The patient started receiving 1 mg of anastrozole daily 6 months prior to presentation and presented with parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes, which is consistent with anastrozole retinopathy.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline retinopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic diseases or other characteristic features of Bietti crystalline retinopathy.

rejected.label: Crystalline retinopathy
rejected.why: This is a more general term and anastrozole retinopathy is a more specific diagnosis that matches the patient's medication history.

rejected.label: Tamoxifen retinopathy
rejected.why: The patient had never previously used tamoxifen, making this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Age-related macular degeneration
rejected.why: The patient's presentation with crystalline deposits is not typical of age-related macular degeneration, and the patient's age and other findings do not strongly support this diagnosis.
